name: e2e_bead_capture_assay_c5: wash, lyse
description: UNROUTED. Built by assay2chip/stages/s6_build.py from partition.json: op 25 wash -> polygon_chamber 'wash_25', op 26 lyse -> polygon_chamber 'lyse_26'. wash, lyse share one board; 6 of the 6 ports allowed at demo scale; 26% of the envelope 30 x 20 mm (demo envelope), ONE fluidic layer at ONE 0.3 mm etch depth, base and lid 0.5 / 1 mm. COP (Zeonor 1060R) because hot_embossing route; DNA adsorption Low: hydrophobic, little DNA binding; protein/enzyme adsorption possible. SIZED FROM THE LOAD, never from the paper's tube volumes (assay2chip/README.md, 'Bench volumes do not transfer'): wash_25 from 2,000 cells at 1500 per uL = 1.33 uL of suspension; lyse_26 from a packed bed of 2,000 x 70 um beads at packing fraction 0.64 = 0.561 uL, then grown to the smallest footprint a channel can attach to (1.40 mm a side). PLACEMENT: parts sit in flow order in 1 row(s) (left to right), spread across the usable 23.6 x 13.6 mm so the slack between them is routing corridor. Total chain length 50.8 mm, crossing risk 0, nothing rotated; every feature keeps at least 0.4 mm to its neighbours and to the chip edge. PORTS: 4 (inlet_1, outlet_1, reagent_in, waste), each over a PORT PAD the registry sized, so the bore opens entirely onto cut area and the port-overlap rule in tools/check_chip_spec.py passes. Inlets and outlets are on opposite edges, which is what keeps the layout planar in one layer, and no two ports are closer than 5 mm. CHANNELS BETWEEN PARTS ARE DELIBERATELY EMPTY: S7 routes them from assay2chip/work/<id>/connections_e2e_bead_capture_assay_c5.json. Until it has run, a chamber here is unconnected on purpose, and every rule that needs a channel - channel width against capsule diameter, channel crossings, protocol targets - can only be checked after S7. Parts sized by assay2chip/parts/registry.py.
